part_2_concurrent_dream_schedulers.verdict: PASS — 15 unique titles, 0 errors, 0 cross-agent state leakage, imagination compounded independently per agent (0.08 vs 0.07)

qualitative_notes: Concurrent SQLite writes via WAL mode showed p95 < 10ms across 50 interleaved writes — no measurable contention.
Both schedulers fired their full quota of dreams during the 60s window (8 + 7 = 15 over ~24s of cycle time each).

Title diversity: 15/15 unique even though both agents pulled from the same seed library — the RNG seeding picks distinct seed combinations even with two agents running back-to-back in the same wall-clock window.
Per-agent snapshot isolation: each agent's imagination trait reflects only its own dream count (0.08 vs 0.07), confirming no cross-writes to lifecycle snapshots.

Real production cadence: agent_a imagination 0.08 over 60s -> ~0.08 trait/min -> imagination would take ~12.5 hours to reach the default min_imagination_trait of 1.0. This is by design (you have to 'earn' the imagination intervention).
